title: Evaluation of the Healing Action of Topical Formulations Based on Libidibia ferrea Fruits in Cutaneous Wounds Induced in Wistar Rats
content: This study investigates the healing action of topical formulations based on Libidibia ferrea fruits in cutaneous wounds induced in Wistar rats. Three types of preparations were evaluated: glycolic extract, infusion, and gel. The phytochemical compounds present in the preparations, such as tannins and flavonoids, are known for their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which are essential for the healing process, histopathological methods evaluated healing, including analysis of epithelialization, granulation tissue formation, and collagen deposition. The results demonstrated that the preparations accelerated the healing process, with a more significant deposition of type I collagen in the groups treated with infusion and glycolic extract, suggesting a more advanced tissue repair process. The infusion demonstrated the best healing results, possibly due to the higher flavonoid content. The findings reinforce the therapeutic potential of Libidibia ferrea in the development of natural healing agents.
